title: 第29章 首次发现间谍

第29章 首次发现间谍-《系统送编，从外卖员成007探员》

望京派出所。

顾承安被领进了一间接待室。

领头民警让他稍坐，然后转身出去了。

门关上之后，走廊里传来一阵低声的交谈。

等了大概五六分钟，领头民警推门进来了。

这次他身后跟了个人——一个四十多岁的男人，短寸头，肩上扛着三级警监的警衔，应该是这个派出所的所长。

顾承安见状，立即起身，恭敬的打了个招呼。

“领导好！”

“你好，别站着了，你坐！”

紧接着又说了一句。

“顾专员，能再次出示下证件吗？”

顾承安爽快的再次掏出证件，他大概也猜到了是什么原因。

所长手里拿着顾承安的证件，脸上的表情很有意思。

刚刚用内部系统查了下对方的姓名，在公安系统里没有找到相关的警员档案，但这不代表就是假的。

由于单警执法记录仪没有拍到警号，不能进一步验证，所以才有了这么一出。

所长接过证件，走到旁边的电脑前，敲了一串编号进去。

屏幕刷新，显示的信息很简短：

姓名：顾承安

职位：公安部督查专员。

警衔：二级警司。

其余档案信息全部加密，备注栏只有一行字：“如需核实，请联系公安部综合督察处。”

虽然知道有这种情况，但现实遇到还是第一次。

他看着顾承安的眼神变得不一样了——这个坐在接待室椅子上、穿着普通看起来跟刚毕业的大学生没什么区别的年轻人，证件级别比他这个干了二十多年的三级警监还要特殊。

“顾专员。”所长的称呼换了，“失敬，失敬。”

顾承安站起来，伸出手：“别客气，今天这事给你们添麻烦了。那个刘卫东涉嫌的情况我已经跟您的同事说了，按正常程序走就行。”

所长握了一下，明显比刚才进来时和气得多了。

“这个自然。不过——”他顿了一下，看着顾承安，“您今天来望京，是路过，还是……”

“路过。”顾承安说，“吃早饭的时候听到的直播，顺手的事。”

所长嘴角抽了一下。

顺手。

公安部督查专员吃早饭的时候顺手拿了个敲诈勒索犯。

Wangjing Police Station.

Gu Chengan was led into a reception room.

The leading police officer asked him to sit down for a moment, then turned around and went out.

After the door closed, there was a murmur of conversation in the corridor.

After waiting for about five or six minutes, the leading police officer pushed open the door and came in.

This time he was followed by someone - a man in his forties with short hair and the title of third-level police officer on his shoulder. He should be the director of the police station.

When Gu Chengan saw this, he immediately stood up and greeted him respectfully.

"Good leader!"

"Hello, stop standing, sit down!"

Then he said something else.

"Commissioner Gu, can you show me your ID again?"

Gu Chengan readily took out his ID card again, and he probably guessed the reason.

The director held Gu Chengan's ID in his hand, with an interesting expression on his face.

I just checked the other party's name using the internal system and found no relevant police officer files in the public security system, but that doesn't mean it's fake.

Since the police signal was not captured by the individual police officer's law enforcement recorder, further verification could not be carried out, so this was the case.

The director took the certificate, walked to the computer next to him, and typed in a number.

The screen refreshes and the message displayed is very brief:

Name: Gu Chengan

Position: Inspector of the Ministry of Public Security.

Police rank: Superintendent II.

The rest of the file information is all encrypted, and there is only one line in the remarks column: "If you need verification, please contact the Comprehensive Inspection Office of the Ministry of Public Security."

Although I know this happens, this is the first time I have encountered it in reality.

His eyes looked different when he looked at Gu Chengan - this young man sitting on the chair in the reception room, wearing ordinary clothes and looking no different from a recent college graduate, had a more special certificate than him, a third-level police superintendent who had worked for more than 20 years.

"Commissioner Gu." The director's title was changed, "Disrespect, disrespect."

Gu Chengan stood up and stretched out his hand: "You're welcome, this matter has caused trouble for you today. I have already told your colleagues about Liu Weidong's alleged situation. Just follow the normal procedures."

The director shook his hand and was obviously much kinder than when he came in just now.

"Of course. But -" he paused and looked at Gu Chengan, "are you passing by Wangjing today, or..."

"Passing by," Gu Chengan said, "I heard the live broadcast while having breakfast. It was a coincidence."

The director's mouth twitched.

smoothly.

The inspector general of the Ministry of Public Security picked up a blackmailer while having breakfast.
